overview: White supports d4 with e3 and develops quietly, avoiding the sharp ...dxc4 theory. Black develops the light bishop with 4...Bf5 (Schallopp) or 4...Bg4, then plays ...e6, ...Nbd7 and ...Be7 with a solid centre. Play is slow and manoeuvring; White seeks a small edge, Black a solid hold and a later ...c5 or ...e5.

white_ideas.idea: Nc3, Bd3 or Nh4 to trade Black's light bishop.
Queenside play with cxd5, Qb3 or a minority attack.

black_ideas.idea: Develop the light bishop outside the chain first, then ...e6 and ...Nbd7.
Break with ...c5 or ...dxc4 and ...e5 to equalise.

typical_structures.structure: Slav triangle c6/d5/e6 with tension on c4/d5.

character.notes: Slow, sound lines where Black has few weaknesses.

structure.notes: Centre in tension, not yet decided.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pin Defense
sublines_that_differ.how: Pins the knight, slightly more active.

character.reason: Slav is hard to break down and play is steady.

plans.reason: No single recognisable plan from the list.
